hiddenCases.name: a different file gives a different answer
pandas does the reading

exercise1.hint: pd.read_csv(path), then the mean of the score column, then round to two places. The second check swaps the file, so a typed-in answer fails.

exercise2.hint: Read once into a variable, then take shape[0], shape[1] and sorted(df.columns) off it.

questions.prompt: What does read_csv do with the first line of the file by default?
choices: Treats it as the column names
questions.explain: header=0 is the default. Pass header=None when the file genuinely has no header row.

questions.prompt: What is worth checking straight after read_csv?
choices: shape, dtypes and the first few rows
questions.explain: Two lines that catch a wrong separator, a missing header and a numeric column read as text.

questions.prompt: read_csv guessed a numeric column as object. What is the likely cause?
choices: At least one value in it is not a number
questions.explain: A column has one dtype, so a single unparseable value takes the whole column to object.

questions.prompt: You read a file and shape says (1000, 1) instead of (1000, 6). What now?
questions.explain: Each line arrived unsplit as a single value. sep= is the argument that fixes it, and nothing raised to tell you.
